newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romanian government credits 16.7 pct up in Dec.
newsitem.headline: Romanian government credits 16.7 pct up in Dec.

text.p: Credits to the Romanian government soared by 16.7 percent to 4.62 trillion lei last December, pushing overall domestic loans up by 8.4 percent from the previous month, central bank data (BNR) showed.
Loans to the government accounted for 14.7 percent of end-1996 domestic credits which stood at 31.46 trillion lei, or 80.8 percent up from end-1995, BNR data showed on Thursday.
Non-government credits rose by 7.1 percent to 26.8 trillion lei last December, with hard currency loans surging by 13 percent to 9.9 trillion lei.
Short-term credits accounted for 83.1 percent of end-1996 leu loans, which stood at 16.94 trillion lei, up from 16.3 trillion the previous month and 11.58 trillion at end-1995.
State companies held 52 percent of leu loans at the end of last year, down from 65.5 percent in 1995.
Inflation was 10.3 percent last December, with the year-on-year rate at 56.9 percent.
